findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract methods such as counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the new build_occurrence_and_event_data. MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits it with only `pass` and implements none of them, so Python treats it as an abstract class. MetricAlertFire.detector_handler is set to this class, and Detector.detector_handler does `group_type.detector_handler(self)`; for a detector of this type, that will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler ...`. Implement the required methods or keep this handler as a concrete non-stateful stub that returns an empty dict.

findings.title: Expected occurrence built with the wrong group key in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe
findings.body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, ...)` creates an occurrence whose fingerprint is `[<detector_id>:val1]`, but the evaluated call uses `expected_result.group_key`, which is `"group_key"` (and value 10). The actual result's occurrence will have fingerprint `[<detector_id>:group_key]`. Since IssueOccurrence is a dataclass and equality includes fingerprint, the assertion comparing the handler result to `expected_result` will fail. Build the expected occurrence with the same group_key/value that will be evaluated.

findings.title: Occurrence produced before detector state is committed; retries can duplicate issues
findings.body: `process_detectors` calls `create_issue_occurrence_from_result` for each result and only afterwards calls `handler.commit_state_updates()` (line 68). If the process crashes or the DB/Redis state commit fails after Kafka production, the dedupe/status state is not advanced. A retry of the same data packet will evaluate the same transition again and emit another occurrence/status change. This is now a real path because stateful detectors return non-None occurrence results. Commit state before producing, or make occurrence production idempotent/transactional.

findings.title: Expected occurrences are built with wrong evaluated values
findings.body: In `test_state_results_multi_group`, `group_2` is evaluated with value 10 from the data packet, but the expected occurrence is built with value 6. The mock `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` currently ignores `value`, so the test passes and does not verify that the hook receives the actual group value. Similar mismatches occur in `test_results_on_change` (evaluates 100, expects 6) and `test_dedupe` (evaluates 8, expects 6). Use the same value as the evaluation so the hook's value argument is covered.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The docstring for `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` says it returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`, but the method now returns `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. This can mislead implementers and callers about the contract.
